text:
Edmonton hosts Vancouver tonight with the Oilers on the better run and the Canucks on the worse one. The Canucks are winless in four (0-4-0 in that stretch, 1-4-0 in their last five) after a 6-2 loss at Winnipeg, and they're without Filip Chytil, with Elias Pettersson taking his spot beside Jonathan Lekkerimäki and Brock Boeser. The Oilers lost 5-4 to Anaheim on Wednesday but are 3-1-1 in their last five. They're missing Zach Hyman, and Colton Dach has stepped into his place on the line with Kasperi Kapanen and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins.

Our numbers favor Edmonton, 3.59 expected goals to 2.55. Expected goals measure the quality of chances. At five on five, Vancouver has taken 41% of them and Edmonton 49%. Edmonton's power play creates 0.88 expected goals a game against a Vancouver penalty kill that allows 0.91, and the Canucks take 4.2 penalties a game. In net, Leevi Meriläinen (projected) is 1.74 goals worse than expected this season and Tristan Jarry (projected) 1.73 worse, though Meriläinen has been rougher lately, 4.1 goals below expected over his last five starts.

Connor McDavid is 95% for a point, riding a 17-game point streak. Leon Draisaitl is 51% to score. For Vancouver, Boeser is 53% for a point and has seven points in six games against Edmonton. We'd also watch Kapanen, one of our under-the-radar picks: he's 50% for a point, up from 39% on his season pace, with more ice time and a Canucks defense that gives up the second-most expected goals per 60. The teams split two high-scoring games in September and October.
